emails.subject: Simulated Acme: when to defend the brand click
emails.body:
Hi Alex,

Similarweb estimates 62% of Simulated Acme's US desktop paid-search visits came from brand terms between 18 Sept and 18 Oct 2026.

That raises a useful bidding question: when does your brand ad need to defend the click, and when could a lower bid do the same job?

How are you making that call today?

Gil

emails.subject: Who appears on "Simulated Acme"?
emails.body:
Hi Alex,

A 19 Oct 2026 desktop check in New York for "Simulated Acme" showed your ad alongside another advertiser.

I'd look at when other advertisers appear and whether your coverage changes with them.

Signal monitors branded Google search conditions and competitor presence.

Would a view of when that query is quiet or contested help your team?

Gil

emails.subject: A focused test for "Simulated Acme"
emails.body:
Hi Alex,

For "Simulated Acme", I'd test whether brand bids can follow competition without giving up conversions.

Signal can lower bids or pause ads where configured, then restore coverage when competition returns.

I'd start with one query, a control and clear conversion guardrails before changing anything more broadly.

Would a short test outline be useful?

Gil

emails.subject: Leave the Simulated Acme brand-bidding question here?
emails.body:
Hi Alex,

I'll leave the Simulated Acme brand-bidding question here.

If adjusting bids around changing competition is already covered, no need to revisit it. If it's still a manual call, I'd be happy to compare approaches.

Gil
